question: In March 2025, who became the first Indian to receive the Ramsar Award for ‘Wetland Wise Use’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jayshree Vencatesan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jayshree Vencatesan** became the first Indian to receive the prestigious **Ramsar Award for 'Wetland Wise Use'** in March 2025.
 
• The Ramsar Award is an international recognition given by the **Ramsar Convention**, which focuses on the conservation and sustainable use of **wetlands** globally.
 
• She is a renowned **environmentalist** and wetland conservationist with extensive contributions to **sustainable wetland management** in India.
 
• Her efforts have led to increased awareness about the importance of **wetlands** in maintaining ecological balance and supporting biodiversity.
 
• Jayshree Vencatesan has worked on projects related to the **protection of wetlands**, such as marshlands, estuaries, and mangroves in India, ensuring their wise use for future generations.
 
• She actively engages with policymakers and local communities to promote **wetland preservation** while integrating sustainable development practices.
 
• The Ramsar Convention, established in **1971**, aims to conserve and use wetlands sustainably, and Jayshree's work aligns with its goals.
 
• This recognition highlights her contributions to wetland conservation and India's growing role in global environmental sustainability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Medha Patkar**__

 __
 
• **Medha Patkar** is a prominent Indian social activist known for her work in the **Narmada Bachao Andolan**, which focused on the displacement caused by dam construction along the Narmada River.
 
• While she has been a vocal advocate for environmental and human rights, her work has primarily revolved around issues related to **large-scale development projects** rather than wetland conservation.
 
 
 
• **Sunita Narain**__
 __
 
• **Sunita Narain** is an Indian environmentalist and director of the **Centre for Science and Environment (CSE)**.
 
• She is known for her work on **climate change, water management, and pollution control**. Her advocacy has significantly influenced environmental policy in India.
 
• While her work overlaps with wetland conservation in terms of water resource management, she is not specifically recognized for efforts in wetland-wise use.
 
 
 
• **Vandana Shiva**__
 
 
• **Vandana Shiva** is an Indian scholar and environmental activist known for her work in **ecological agriculture** and the protection of biodiversity.
 
• She has contributed significantly to the movement against **genetically modified organisms (GMOs)** and industrial agriculture.
 
• Her work is more focused on **agriculture and food systems** rather than the conservation of wetlands.
